questions.q: What did David prepare for the Box of God in the City of David?
questions.a: David prepared a place for the Box of God and set up a tent for it.

questions.q: Who did David say were the only people that Yahweh had chosen to carry the Box of Yahweh?
questions.a: The Levites were the only people whom Yahweh had chosen to carry the Box of Yahweh.

questions.q: For what purpose did David assemble all of Israel at Jerusalem?
questions.a: David assembled them to bring up the Box of Yahweh to the place he had prepared for it.

questions.q: Who did David gather together to bring up the Box of Yahweh?
questions.a: David gathered together the descendants of Aaron and the Levites.

questions.q: Who was the chief of the descendants of Kohath, and how many kinsmen did he have with him?
questions.a: Uriel was the chief of the descendants of Kohath, and he had 120 kinsmen with him.

questions.q: Who was the chief of the descendants of Merari, and how many kinsmen did he have with him?
questions.a: Asaiah was the chief of the descendants of Merari, and he had 220 kinsmen with him.

questions.q: Who was the chief of the descendants of Gershom, and how many kinsmen did he have with him?
questions.a: Joel was the chief of the descendants of Gershom, and he had 130 kinsmen with him.

questions.q: Who was the chief of the descendants of Elizaphan, and how many kinsmen did he have with him?
questions.a: Shemaiah was the chief of the descendants of Elizaphan, and he had 200 kinsmen with him.

questions.q: Who was the chief of the descendants of Hebron, and how many kinsmen did he have with him?
questions.a: Eliel was the chief of the descendants of Hebron, and he had 80 kinsmen with him.

questions.q: Who was the chief of the descendants of Uzziel, and how many kinsmen did he have with him?
questions.a: Amminadab was the chief of the descendants of Uzziel, and he had 112 kinsmen with him.

questions.q: Which two priests did David call, along with the leaders of the Levites?
questions.a: David called the priests Zadok and Abiathar, along with the Levites.

questions.q: What were the leaders of the Levite families and their brothers to do so that they could bring up the Box of Yahweh, the God of Israel, to the place David had prepared for it?
questions.a: They were to consecrate themselves so they could bring up the Box of Yahweh, the God of Israel.

questions.q: According to David, what did Yahweh do because the people did not have the Levites carry the Box the first time?
questions.a: According to David, Yahweh their God punished them.

questions.q: Why did the priests and Levites consecrate themselves?
questions.a: They consecrated themselves so that they could bring up the Box of Yahweh, the God of Israel.

questions.q: From whom did Moses get the rules for carrying the Box of God on the Levites’ shoulders with the poles?
questions.a: The rules for carrying the Box of God were given by the word of Yahweh.

questions.q: To whom did David give the responsibility of assigning the musicians?
questions.a: David gave the responsibility of assigning the musicians to the leaders of the Levites.

questions.q: Which three men did the Levites station to lead the singers?
questions.a: The Levites stationed Heman, Asaph, and Ethan.

questions.q: What job did Obed Edom and Jeiel have?
questions.a: Obed Edom and Jeiel were gatekeepers and were appointed to guard the sacred chest.

questions.q: What instrument did Heman, Asaph, and Ethan play?
questions.a: Heman, Asaph, and Ethan played bronze cymbals.

questions.q: What instrument did Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah play?
questions.a: They played lyres.

questions.q: What instrument did Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed Edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah play to lead the music?
questions.a: They played lyres to lead the music.

questions.q: What was Chenaniah’s responsibility among the Levites?
questions.a: Chenaniah was responsible for directing the singing because he understood it well.

questions.q: What job did Berechiah and Elkanah have?
questions.a: Berechiah and Elkanah were keepers of the Box.

questions.q: What were the seven priests doing in front of the Box of God?
questions.a: The seven priests were blowing trumpets in front of the Box of God.

questions.q: Who went to bring up the Box of the Covenant of Yahweh from the house of Obed Edom?
questions.a: David, the elders of Israel, and the commanders of thousands went to bring it up with rejoicing.

questions.q: Who helped the Levites who carried the Box of the Covenant of Yahweh?
questions.a: God helped the Levites who carried the Box of the Covenant of Yahweh.

questions.q: With what was David clothed and what was he wearing in addition?
questions.a: David was clothed in a robe of fine linen, and he was wearing a linen ephod.

questions.q: Who brought up the Box of the Covenant of Yahweh with joyful shouting, with the sound of horns and trumpets, with cymbals, and with lyres and harps?
questions.a: All of Israel brought up the Box of the Covenant of Yahweh.

questions.q: What did Michal see David doing that caused her to despise him in her heart?
questions.a: Michal saw King David dancing and celebrating.

commentary.text: Preparations for the removal of the ark.

Verses 1–24 Wise and good men may be guilty of oversights, which they will correct, as soon as they are aware of them. David does not try to justify what had been done amiss, nor to lay the blame on others; but he owns himself guilty, with others, of not seeking God in due order

It is good to notice the assistance of Divine Providence, even in things which fall within the compass of our natural powers; if God did not help us, we could not stir a step. If we do our religious duties in any degree aright, we must own it was God that helped us; had we been left to ourselves, we should have been guilty of some fatal errors. And every thing in which we engage, must be done in dependence on the mercy of God through the sacrifice of the Redeemer.
